newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Mig sees better '97 after weak '96.
newsitem.headline: San Mig sees better '97 after weak '96.

text.p: The Philippines' leading beer maker San Miguel Corp on Wednesday reported a marginal rise in net income for 1996 and hoped the current year would bring bigger growth.
The firm reported net income of 6.09 billion pesos in 1996, up four percent from 5.84 billion in the previous year.

But the 1996 figure was bolstered by extraordinary gains coming from the sale of certain assets and a second-quarter write-back of 561 million pesos of provisions made in previous years, San Miguel said in a statement.
Excluding the extraordinary gains, San Miguel's 1996 net income declined by two percent to 5.26 billion pesos from 5.38 billion in 1995, or to 2.57 pesos per share from 2.63, the company said.
Consolidated income from operations totalled 9.50 billion pesos compared to 9.40 billion in 1995.
San Miguel said an increase in sales volume and decline in raw material prices raised operating income by 25 percent in the fourth quarter.
The year-end improvement helped reverse what had been a seven percent decline in operating income for the first nine months of the year, it said.
Aggregate sales volume for the year rose by four percent.
San Miguel, which also has interests in liquor, soft drinks, food and packaging, said it hoped for better times this year.
"1997 earnings are expected to exhibit significant growth. Marketing and distribution programmes are aimed at increasing volumes by over 10 percent," the firm said.
The company also expects to benefit from various actions taken in the past year to make its operations more efficient, cost competitive and responsive to the market, it said.
Last year, San Miguel spent money on various expansion projects, including four new breweries overseas.
As a result, financing charges jumped by 92 percent to 2.64 billion pesos from 1.38 billion pesos, San Miguel said.
San Miguel said beer sales in the second half of 1996 were boosted by new marketing initiatives, a slowing down of inflation and a recovery in the agricultural sector.
A large chunk of San Miguel's beer market is in rural areas and its sales are directly linked to farm incomes.
To make up for an erosion in the local beer market, San Miguel launched an overseas expansion, concentrating mainly on China, the company said.
San Miguel said its international beer operations showed an operating loss of 671 million pesos as a result of intensified spending on brand and market development.
Besides three joint venture firms in various provinces of China, San Miguel also has a presence in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Vietnam and Taiwan.

San Miguel said its unit Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, the local franchise holder for Coca-Cola, registered an increase of 14 percent in sales volume in 1996. Its revenue grew 20 percent to 26.3 billion pesos and operating income rose 13 percent to 4.64 billion pesos.
Liquor unit La Tondena Distillers also showed increased sales, but not because of its main product.
Liquor sales growth slowed but vigorous growth in its mineral water business and the acquisition of a juice business helped raise sales volume by 21 percent, San Miguel said.
La Tondena's operating income rose 36 percent to 1.54 billion pesos, it said.
